chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was with him about prostrating on the back of a camel and on pitch (bitumen). He said, 'There is no harm in it.' For it is to be understood as being in a state of necessity or precaution (taqiyyah), and it is not permissible with choice. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to prostrate on impure surfaces like a camel's back or pitch in prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that prostrating on impure surfaces like camel back or pitch is valid but primarily intended for times of necessity (*darurah*) or precaution (*tawqiyyah*), rather than being the preferred practice when one has a choice. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of balancing ritual purity with practical feasibility, ensuring the validity of prayer even when ideal conditions are not met.
